requirements.requirement: Establish an AIDE-based file integrity baseline covering /etc on node1
requirements.summary: aide installed via dnf; /etc/aide.conf verified to have explicit per-path rules plus a catch-all `/etc PERMS` rule covering all of /etc; aide --init created a 39,334-entry database, activated as /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz, and an immediate aide --check reported no differences, confirming a clean established baseline.

requirements.requirement: Baseline must allow later changes to /etc to be identified and reported
requirements.summary: Executor added two test files under /etc and re-ran aide --check, which reported 'Added entries: 2', directly demonstrating that the baseline detects and reports later filesystem changes. Test artifacts were then removed and a clean re-check confirmed restoration to baseline state.

requirements.requirement: Baseline data persists and remains usable across a system restart (durability of the established baseline)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart state captured (boot_id 377b5195..., clean aide check, recorded db checksum). Node was rebooted (systemctl reboot), became unreachable then reachable again with a new boot_id (7e980b46...) and reset uptime, proving a genuine restart. Post-restart, the aide database file and SHA256 checksum were unchanged and a fresh aide --check against it still reported no differences, and the aide package remained installed.

overall_summary: The executor established a functioning AIDE integrity baseline covering all of /etc on node1, empirically validated that it detects and reports added files, and demonstrated the baseline's persistence and continued functionality across a full system restart with direct boot-identity, service, and data-state evidence before and after the reboot. All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence. Minor hygiene deductions are limited to a leftover config backup file and two small log files left under /tmp.
limitations: Full contents of /etc/aide.conf were not shown in evidence beyond the summarized per-path and catch-all rules, so completeness of coverage relies on the executor's grep output and summary rather than a full file dump.

No independent evidence beyond the executor's own commands confirms the /etc/aide.conf.orig backup and /tmp log files are the only residue; broader filesystem-wide residue outside the observed /tmp inventory was not directly checked.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command trace shows a coherent, well-scoped sequence: install aide, back up the stock config (/etc/aide.conf.orig, cmd-386d32686eb145e6) before conditionally modifying it, initialize/activate the database, run a bounded falsification test by adding two files under /etc (cmd-59c9501bc8e5414e) that were explicitly required to validate the change-detection requirement, then remove them and reconfirm a clean state. The restart protocol (cmd-fae1b40aa73541c2, cmd-e6d925be44984720, cmd-bea8eca72f2d4887, cmd-40da9cbd6eeb46f5, cmd-91ab45e92e014c0d) is a low-risk, single planned reboot with clear pre/post verification. Minor residue: the /etc/aide.conf.orig backup file was left in place (harmless but unused since no grep-append occurred), and /tmp/aide-check-after-change.log and /tmp/reboot.log were left in /tmp per the after-executor snapshot diff — both are small, non-sensitive, bounded artifacts rather than broad or destructive residue, so they lower the score only slightly.
